questions.question: Which of the following statements about Newton’s third law of motion is incorrect?

options.text: The action and reaction forces act on the same object.
The forces act simultaneously on two different objects.
When one object exerts a force on another, the second object exerts an equal and opposite force back.
The forces are equal in magnitude but opposite in direction.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The action and reaction forces act on the same object.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton’s Third Law of Motion** states that for every **action**, there is always an **equal and opposite reaction**. This means that forces always exist in pairs.
 
• A fundamental requirement of this law is that the **action and reaction forces act on two different objects**. If they acted on the **same object**, the **net force** would always be **zero**, making it impossible for any individual object to **accelerate** or change its state of motion. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The forces involved in the interaction act **simultaneously**. There is no time delay or "cause and effect" lag between the **action** and the **reaction**; they happen at the exact same moment. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• When one object (Object A) exerts a **force** on another (Object B), the second object (Object B) instantaneously exerts a **force** back on the first (Object A). ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• These two forces are **equal in magnitude** but **opposite in direction**. This is why the law is often expressed mathematically using **vectors** as **Fab = -Fba**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is that the statement "The action and reaction forces act on the same object" is the incorrect one.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sir Isaac Newton**: He formulated the three laws of motion and published them in his monumental work, **"Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica"**, in the year **1687**. These laws form the basis of **Classical Mechanics**.
 
• **Newton's First Law (Law of Inertia)**: It states that an object will remain at **rest** or continue to move at a **constant velocity** unless acted upon by an external **unbalanced force**.
 
• **Newton's Second Law**: It establishes that the **force (F)** acting on an object is equal to the **mass (m)** of the object multiplied by its **acceleration (a)**, commonly expressed as **F = ma**. It also defines force as the rate of change of **momentum**.
 
• **Practical Examples of the Third Law**:
 
 
• **Recoil of a Gun**: When a bullet is fired (action), the gun pushes back on the shoulder of the shooter (reaction).
 
• **Walking**: To walk forward, a person pushes the ground backward with their foot (action), and the ground pushes the person forward (reaction).
 
• **Propulsion of a Rocket**: The rocket engine expels hot exhaust gases downward (action), and the gases exert an upward thrust on the rocket (reaction), allowing it to lift off.
 
• **Swimming**: A swimmer pushes the water backward (action), and the water pushes the swimmer forward (reaction).
 
 
 
• **Force Measurement**: The **SI unit** of force is the **Newton (N)**. **One Newton** is defined as the force required to accelerate a mass of **1 kilogram** at a rate of **1 meter per second squared (1 kg·m/s²)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cancellation of Forces**: A common misconception is that because the forces are equal and opposite, they should cancel each other out. However, **cancellation** only occurs when multiple forces act on the **same single body**. Since action-reaction pairs act on **different bodies**, they do not cancel each other.
 
• **Mass and Acceleration**: While the forces are equal in magnitude, the resulting **accelerations** of the two objects may be very different depending on their **masses** (as per the **Second Law**). For example, the Earth pulls on a falling apple with the same force the apple pulls on the Earth, but the Earth's massive **inertia** means its acceleration is negligible.

questions.question: A wire of resistivity rho , has a length L and area of cross-section A . If the resistance of the wire is R , then which of the following is the correct relation for R ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**R = ρL/A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **electrical resistance (R)** of a conductor is defined as the opposition offered by the conductor to the flow of **electric current** through it.
 
• It has been experimentally observed that the **resistance** of a uniform metallic conductor is **directly proportional** to its **length (L)**. This means that as the length of the wire increases, the resistance increases proportionally. ***Hence, the numerator must contain L.***
 
• The **resistance** is also **inversely proportional** to the **area of cross-section (A)** of the conductor. A larger cross-sectional area allows more electrons to flow, thereby reducing the resistance. ***Hence, the denominator must contain A.***
 
• The **resistivity (ρ)**, also known as **specific resistance**, is a constant of proportionality that depends on the **nature of the material** and the **temperature**. It is a fundamental property of a material that quantifies how strongly it resists or conducts electric current.
 
• By combining these dependencies, we arrive at the mathematical relation: **R = ρ (L / A)**. This formula is used to calculate the resistance of any linear conductor when its physical dimensions and material properties are known. ***Hence, the correct relation is R = ρL/A.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SI Units:**
 
 
• The **SI unit** of **resistance (R)** is the **Ohm**, represented by the Greek symbol **Ω**.
 
• The **SI unit** of **resistivity (ρ)** is the **Ohm-meter (Ω·m)**.
 
• **Length (L)** is measured in **meters (m)**, and **Area (A)** is measured in **square meters (m²)**.
 
 
 
• **Nature of Materials:**
 
 
• **Conductors**, such as **Silver**, **Copper**, and **Aluminium**, have very low resistivity, typically in the range of **10^-8 Ω·m** to **10^-6 Ω·m**.
 
• **Insulators** like **Rubber**, **Glass**, and **Ebonite** have very high resistivity, often ranging from **10^12 Ω·m** to **10^17 Ω·m**.
 
• **Alloys** like **Constantan** and **Manganin** have higher resistivity than their constituent metals and are often used to make standard resistors because their resistance does not change significantly with temperature.
 
 
 
• **Conductance and Conductivity:**
 
 
• The reciprocal of resistance is called **Conductance (G)**, measured in **Siemens (S)** or **mho**.
 
• The reciprocal of resistivity is called **Electrical Conductivity (σ)**, which measures the ability of a material to conduct electricity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Effect of Temperature:** For most **metallic conductors**, the resistance and resistivity increase with an **increase in temperature**. However, for **semiconductors** (like Silicon and Germanium), the resistance decreases as the temperature rises.
 
• **Stretching a Wire:** If a wire of resistance **R** is stretched to **n** times its original length, its new resistance becomes **n²R**. This is because while the **length (L)** increases, the **area of cross-section (A)** decreases simultaneously to keep the **volume** constant.
 
• **Resistivity vs Resistance:** It is important to note that while **resistance** depends on the **shape and size** (length and area) of the conductor, **resistivity** is independent of dimensions and depends only on the **material** and **temperature**.
 
• **Ohm's Law:** This relation is often used in conjunction with **Ohm's Law (V = IR)**, where **V** is the potential difference and **I** is the current flowing through the conductor.

questions.question: Which method is commonly used to prevent rusting of Iron?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Galvanisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Galvanisation** is a widely used method to protect **Iron** and **Steel** from **corrosion** or **rusting** by applying a thin protective layer of **Zinc**.
 
• The process typically involves **Hot-Dip Galvanizing**, where the metal component is submerged in a bath of **molten Zinc** at a temperature of approximately **450°C** (**842°F**).
 
• The **Zinc** coating acts as a **physical barrier**, preventing **Oxygen** and **moisture** (water) from reaching the **Iron** surface, which are the two primary requirements for rust formation.
 
• Even if the coating is damaged or scratched, the **Zinc** provides **cathodic protection** by acting as a **sacrificial anode**; it corrodes in preference to the **Iron** because **Zinc** is more **chemically active**.
 
• Common applications of this method include **G.I. pipes** (Galvanised Iron), **roofing sheets**, **nails**, **screws**, **fencing wire**, and **structural steel** used in construction. ***Hence, the correct answer is Galvanisation.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Chemistry of Rusting**: 
 
 
• **Rusting** is an **oxidation reaction** where **Iron** reacts with **Oxygen** in the presence of **water** to form **Hydrated Iron (III) Oxide** (**Fe2O3·nH2O**).
 
• Unlike the oxide layer on **Aluminum**, rust is **porous** and flaky; it does not protect the underlying metal but instead promotes further **corrosion**.
 
 
 
• **Alloying**:
 
 
• This involves mixing **Iron** with other elements like **Chromium** and **Nickel** to produce **Stainless Steel**. 
 
• The **Chromium** (usually at least **10.5%**) reacts with **Oxygen** to form a very thin, **invisible**, and **self-healing** layer of **Chromium Oxide** that prevents rust.
 
 
 
• **Other Protective Methods**:
 
 
• **Painting**: Provides a simple **barrier**; commonly used for **bridges**, **ships**, and **cars**.
 
• **Greasing and Oiling**: Used for **moving machine parts** and **tools** where paint cannot be applied; it displaces moisture.
 
• **Electroplating**: Using **electricity** to deposit a layer of metals like **Tin**, **Chromium**, or **Nickel** on the surface of **Iron** objects.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Options**:
 
 
• **Magnetising**: This is the process of making a substance **magnetic** and has no effect on the chemical process of **rusting**.
 
• **Melting**: This is a **physical change** from solid to liquid and does not offer any long-term protection against **oxidation**.
 
• **Heating**: Exposure to high heat in the presence of air can actually **accelerate** the formation of **metal oxides** rather than preventing them.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **rate of rusting** is significantly higher in **coastal areas** because the **saltwater** (saline water) contains **ions** that increase the **electrical conductivity** of the water film on the metal, speeding up the **electrochemical reaction**.
 
• **Zinc** has an **atomic number** of **30** and is placed higher than **Iron** (**atomic number 26**) in the **Reactivity Series** of metals.
 
• **Anodizing** is a similar electrochemical process but is specifically used to thicken the natural **oxide layer** on **Aluminum** surfaces to increase **durability**.
 
• The **Iron Pillar of Delhi**, built in the **4th century CE**, is a world-famous example of **corrosion resistance** achieved through specific **metallurgical compositions** (high phosphorus content) rather than modern **Galvanisation**.

questions.question: Which of the following feature enables muscular tissue to produce movement in animals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Presence of contractile proteins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muscular tissue** consists of elongated cells, also known as **muscle fibers**. This tissue is responsible for all types of movement within the body of an animal.
 
• Muscles contain special proteins called **contractile proteins**, which contract and relax to cause movement. The two primary types of these proteins are **actin** and **myosin**.
 
• When these proteins slide over one another, the muscle cell shortens, leading to **contraction**. When they return to their original position, it leads to **relaxation**. This coordinated cycle is the fundamental mechanism of **locomotion** and internal physical functions.
 
• Regarding the other options provided in the question:
 
 
• **Storage of fat droplets**: This is a primary function of **adipose tissue**, which acts as an energy reservoir and insulator. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Presence of contractile proteins**: These are the mechanical engines of the muscle cell that facilitate physical displacement and force. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Ability to transmit nerve impulses**: While muscles respond to electrical signals, the actual **transmission** of impulses over long distances is the specialized function of **nervous tissue** (neurons). ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Secretion of digestive enzymes**: This is a function performed by **epithelial tissue**, specifically glandular epithelium found in the stomach, pancreas, and intestines. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Muscular Tissue**:
 
 
• **Striated Muscle (Skeletal Muscle)**: These are **voluntary muscles** mostly attached to bones. Under a microscope, they show alternate light and dark bands or **striations**. They are long, cylindrical, unbranched, and **multinucleated**.
 
• **Smooth Muscle (Unstriated Muscle)**: These are **involuntary muscles** found in the walls of hollow internal organs such as the **alimentary canal**, **blood vessels**, and the **iris** of the eye. They are spindle-shaped (tapering at ends) and have a single **nucleus**.
 
• **Cardiac Muscle**: These are found exclusively in the **heart**. They are **involuntary**, cylindrical, **branched**, and uninucleated. They show rhythmic contraction and relaxation throughout the **lifespan** of the animal without getting fatigued.
 
 
 
• **Mechanism of Movement**:
 
 
• The **Sliding Filament Theory** is the most widely accepted explanation for muscle contraction. It states that the thick (myosin) and thin (actin) filaments slide past each other, decreasing the length of the **sarcomere** (the functional unit of contraction).
 
• Muscle contraction is often triggered by **Calcium ions (Ca2+)** released from the **sarcoplasmic reticulum** following a stimulus from the nervous system.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sarcomere**: It is defined as the segment between two neighboring **Z-lines** and is considered the basic unit of a muscle's cross-striated myofibril.
 
• **Excitability**: This is the ability of muscle tissue to receive and respond to **stimuli**, which distinguishes it from other connective tissues.
 
• **Energy Requirement**: Muscle contraction is an active process that requires a significant amount of **Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP)**, which is why muscle cells contain a high number of **mitochondria**.
 
• **Locomotion vs. Movement**: While movement refers to the change in position of any part of the body, **locomotion** specifically refers to the movement of the entire animal from one **location** to another.
</ul

questions.question: What will the distance-time graph look like for an object moving with uniform speed?

options.text: The graph looks like a sine wave.
The graph is a zig zag line.
The graph is a straight line.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The graph is a straight line**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• For an object moving with **uniform speed**, the **distance** traveled is **directly proportional** to the **time** taken. This linear relationship ensures that as time increases, the distance increases at a **constant rate**.
 
• In a **distance-time graph**, **time** is typically plotted on the **X-axis** (independent variable) and **distance** is plotted on the **Y-axis** (dependent variable).
 
• The **slope** of a distance-time graph represents the **speed** of the object. Since the speed is **uniform** (constant), the slope remains the same at every point on the graph, which mathematically results in a **straight line**.
 
• A **straight line** passing through the **origin** (0,0) indicates that the object was at the **reference starting point** at **time zero** and moved with a constant velocity thereafter. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• A **sine wave** graph represents **oscillatory** or **periodic motion**, such as a pendulum, where the position varies harmonically over time. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• A **zig-zag line** represents **non-uniform motion** where the speed and direction change abruptly and inconsistently. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uniform Motion:**
 
 
• An object is said to be in **uniform motion** if it covers **equal distances** in **equal intervals of time**, no matter how small these time intervals may be.
 
• In this state, the **acceleration** of the object is **zero** because the velocity does not change in magnitude or direction.
 
 
 
• **Non-Uniform Motion:**
 
 
• If an object covers **unequal distances** in **equal intervals of time**, it is in **non-uniform motion**.
 
• The **distance-time graph** for non-uniform motion is a **curved line**, indicating that the speed is changing (accelerating or decelerating).
 
 
 
• **Object at Rest:**
 
 
• When an object is **stationary**, its distance from the reference point does not change as time passes.
 
• The **distance-time graph** for an object at rest is a **horizontal straight line** parallel to the **time-axis (X-axis)**, where the slope is **zero**.
 
 
 
• **Speed Calculation from Graph:**
 
 
• To find the speed from a distance-time graph, one can pick any two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) on the line and calculate the **gradient**.
 
• The formula used is **Speed = (Distance2 - Distance1) / (Time2 - Time1)**. For a straight line, this value will always be **constant**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Steepness of the Graph:** The **steepness** or **gradient** of the straight line indicates the **magnitude of speed**. A steeper line represents a **higher speed**, while a flatter line represents a **lower speed**.
 
• **Physical Constraints:** A **distance-time graph** can never be a **vertical line** parallel to the Y-axis. This would imply the object is covering distance in **zero time**, which means it has **infinite speed**—a physical impossibility in classical mechanics.
 
• **Comparison:** By plotting distance-time lines for two different objects on the same graph, one can easily compare their **relative speeds** by looking at which line is **closer to the Y-axis** (steeper).
 
• **Units:** Standard **SI units** used in these graphs are **meters (m)** for distance and **seconds (s)** for time, making the unit of the slope (speed) **m/s**.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true regarding a concave lens?

(i) A concave lens is also called a diverging lens.
(ii) A concave lens always forms a real and inverted image of the object placed anywhere in front of it.
(iii) A concave lens always forms a virtual and erect image of the object placed anywhere in front of it.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (i) and (iii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave lens** is an optical device that is thinner at the **center** than at the **edges**. It is fundamentally known as a **diverging lens** because it causes parallel rays of light to spread out or diverge after passing through it. ***Hence, statement (i) is correct.***
 
• The divergence of light rays means they never meet on the opposite side of the lens; instead, they appear to originate from a single point called the **principal focus** on the same side as the object.
 
• A concave lens always produces a **virtual**, **erect**, and **diminished** image, regardless of where the object is placed. It cannot form a **real and inverted** image because the refracted rays do not actually intersect. ***Hence, statement (ii) is incorrect.***
 
• Because the image is always formed by the apparent intersection of light rays, it is categorized as **virtual**. Since the image is oriented in the same direction as the object, it is described as **erect**. ***Hence, statement (iii) is correct.***
 
• ***Therefore, the correct answer is Both (i) and (iii).***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Optical Characteristics**: 
 
 
• The **focal length** of a concave lens is considered **negative** according to the **Cartesian sign convention**.
 
• The **power** of a concave lens is also **negative**, expressed in **Dioptres (D)**. For example, a prescription of **-2.0 D** indicates a concave lens.
 
 
 
• **Image Positions**:
 
 
• If an object is placed at **infinity**, the image is formed at the **focus (F1)**, being highly diminished and point-sized.
 
• If the object is between **infinity and the optical center (O)**, the image is formed between the focus and the optical center on the same side as the object.
 
 
 
• **Common Applications**:
 
 
• **Spectacles**: These lenses are the primary tool used to correct **Myopia** (nearsightedness), helping the eye focus light correctly on the **retina**.
 
• **Flashlights**: They are used to diverge the light beam to cover a larger area.
 
• **Peepholes**: Installed in doors to provide a **diminished** but wide-angle view of the area outside.
 
• **Telescopes**: Often used in the eyepieces of **Galilean telescopes** to provide an upright image.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lens Formula**: The mathematical relationship between **object distance (u)**, **image distance (v)**, and **focal length (f)** is given by the formula **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**.
 
• **Magnification (m)**: It is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object, or **m = v/u**. For a concave lens, the magnification is always **positive** and **less than 1**, indicating the image is virtual and smaller than the object.
 
• **Refractive Index**: The degree of divergence depends on the **refractive index** of the material (like **glass** or **plastic**) and the curvature of the lens surfaces.
 
• **Comparison**: Unlike a **convex lens** (converging lens), which can form **real**, **inverted**, **magnified**, or **virtual** images based on the object's position, the concave lens is much more limited and consistent in its image properties.
</ul

questions.question: A student wants to separate a heterogeneous mixture of mud and water collected from a pond. Based on your understanding of mixtures, which method would be most effective and why?

options.text: Chromatography, because it separates based on movement in a medium
Distillation, because it separates based on boiling points
Evaporation, because it removes the solvent
Filtration, because the solid particles in mud are not dissolved in water

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Filtration, because the solid particles in mud are not dissolved in water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Filtration** is a physical separation method used to remove **insoluble solid particles** from a liquid or gas by passing the mixture through a **porous medium** (like filter paper).
 
• A mixture of mud and water is a **heterogeneous mixture** (specifically a **suspension**), meaning the components are not uniformly distributed and the solid mud particles do not dissolve in the water. ***Hence, the statement provided in option 4 is correct.***
 
• During this process, the clear liquid that passes through the filter is called the **filtrate**, while the solid particles trapped on the filter medium are referred to as the **residue**.
 
• This method is highly effective for pond water because the **particle size** of mud is significantly larger than the **pore size** of standard filtration media, ensuring a clear separation without needing heat or chemical additives.
 
• Unlike methods that involve phase changes, filtration preserves both the solid and the liquid components in their original states, making it efficient for large volumes of **muddy water**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Evaporation:**
 
 
• This method involves heating the mixture until the **solvent** (water) turns into **vapor**, leaving the **solute** (mud) behind.
 
• While it separates the mud, it is less "effective" for general separation because the water is lost to the atmosphere unless a **condenser** is used. It is typically used for **homogeneous mixtures** like salt and water.
 
 
 
• **Distillation:**
 
 
• **Distillation** is a process that separates components based on differences in their **boiling points**.
 
• It is primarily used to separate **miscible liquids** (like alcohol and water) or to obtain pure water from a salt solution. Using it for mud and water is unnecessarily complex and energy-intensive compared to filtration.
 
 
 
• **Chromatography:**
 
 
• This technique is used to separate components of a mixture based on their different rates of **movement** through a **stationary phase** under the influence of a **mobile phase**.
 
• It is used for separating **dyes, pigments, or chemicals** in a solution, rather than separating bulk solids like mud from water.
 
 
 
• **Heterogeneous vs. Homogeneous Mixtures:**
 
 
• **Heterogeneous mixtures** (e.g., mud in water, oil in water) have visible boundaries of separation.
 
• **Homogeneous mixtures** (e.g., sugar in water, air) have a uniform composition throughout and cannot be separated by simple filtration.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sedimentation and Decantation:** Before filtration, a mixture of mud and water can be left undisturbed to allow the heavier mud particles to settle at the bottom due to **gravity**; this is **sedimentation**. The clear water can then be poured out, which is **decantation**. Filtration is often the final step after these to ensure total clarity.
 
• **Loading:** Sometimes, very fine mud particles stay suspended. To speed up sedimentation, **Alum** (potash alum) is added. This process is called **loading**, where the alum particles attach to the fine dirt, making them heavy enough to sink.
 
• **Applications:** Filtration is a critical step in **municipal water treatment plants**, where large-scale **sand filters** are used to provide potable water to cities. In daily life, it is used in **tea strainers** and **HEPA filters** in vacuum cleaners to trap dust.
</ul

questions.question: A ball is thrown up with a velocity of x m/s. The ball attains a maximum height of 50 m. What is the value of x? (Take the value of g as 10 m/s²)

The correct answer is __**10√10 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The problem describes a case of **vertical motion under gravity**, which is a form of **uniformly accelerated motion** where the acceleration is constant.
 
• When an object is thrown vertically upward, its **velocity** decreases until it reaches the highest point. At this **maximum height**, the **final velocity (v)** of the object becomes **0 m/s**.
 
• To find the **initial velocity (x)**, we use the **third equation of motion**: **v² = u² + 2as**. In this context, **u** is the **initial velocity (x)**, **v** is the **final velocity (0 m/s)**, **a** is the **acceleration due to gravity (-g)**, and **s** is the **maximum height (H)**.
 
• Given values are **maximum height (H) = 50 m** and **acceleration due to gravity (g) = 10 m/s²**. Because the ball is moving upward against the pull of gravity, the acceleration is taken as **-10 m/s²**.
 
• Substituting the values into the equation: **0² = x² + 2(-10)(50)**. This simplifies to **0 = x² - 1000**.
 
• Solving for **x**, we get **x² = 1000**, which means **x = √1000**. This can be simplified to **x = √(100 × 10)**, resulting in **x = 10√10 m/s**. ***Hence, the calculated value of initial velocity is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The first equation is **v = u + at**, used to find velocity or time.
 
• The second equation is **s = ut + (1/2)at²**, used to determine the **displacement** of an object over a period of **time**.
 
• The third equation is **v² = u² + 2as**, which is independent of time and relates velocity directly to displacement.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity (g):**
 
 
• This is the **acceleration** gained by an object due to the **gravitational force** of the Earth.
 
• Its standard value is approximately **9.8 m/s²** at sea level, but for competitive exams and simplified calculations, it is often taken as **10 m/s²**.
 
• The value of **g** varies slightly depending on **altitude** and **latitude**, being higher at the poles and lower at the equator.
 
 
 
• **Maximum Height (H):**
 
 
• The **maximum height** attained by a projectile or a vertically thrown object occurs when its **kinetic energy** is fully converted into **potential energy** (neglecting air resistance).
 
• The formula derived from the equations of motion for maximum height is **H = u² / (2g)**.
 
• If the **initial velocity** is doubled, the **maximum height** will increase by **four times**, following the square relationship.

Since **gravity** always acts downward, **g** is treated as **negative** when an object is thrown **upward**.
 
• **Mass Independence:** In a **vacuum** (where air resistance is zero), the **maximum height** reached by an object depends only on its **initial velocity** and **gravity**, not on its **mass**. A heavy ball and a light ball thrown with the same **velocity** will reach the same **height**.

questions.question: Lenses are used in spectacles to correct vision because they work on the principle of __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Refraction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Refraction** is the fundamental optical principle where **light rays bend** when they pass from one transparent medium to another of different **optical density**, such as from **air** into a **glass** or **plastic lens**.
 
• Spectacle lenses are designed with specific **curvatures** to utilize refraction to redirect light. This ensures that the light rays entering the eye are properly **focused** directly onto the **retina**, rather than in front of or behind it.
 
• The degree of bending depends on the **refractive index** of the lens material and the **angle of incidence**. Corrective lenses use materials with a higher refractive index than air to achieve the desired vision correction.
 
• This principle is governed by **Snell’s Law**, which describes the relationship between the angles of incidence and refraction. ***Hence, the correct answer is Refraction.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Myopia (Nearsightedness)**:
 
 
• In this condition, the eyeball is too long or the cornea is too curved, causing light to focus **in front of the retina**.
 
• It is corrected using a **Concave Lens** (diverging lens), which spreads the light rays before they reach the eye, moving the focal point back onto the **retina**.
 
 
 
• **Hypermetropia (Farsightedness)**:
 
 
• In this case, light focuses **behind the retina** because the eyeball is too short or the lens lacks sufficient converging power.
 
• A **Convex Lens** (converging lens) is used to bend the light rays inward earlier, allowing them to converge exactly on the **retinal surface**.
 
 
 
• **Other Optical Principles (Incorrect Options)**:
 
 
• **Reflection**: This is the bouncing back of light when it hits a surface. While **mirrors** work on reflection, lenses do not rely on this to correct vision. ***Statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Polarization**: This process involves filtering light waves to vibrate in a single plane. It is used in **sunglasses** to reduce **glare** from reflective surfaces like water or roads, but it does not correct refractive errors. ***Statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Diffraction**: This is the slight bending of light as it passes around the edge of an object or through an opening. It is not the principle used for standard vision correction in spectacles. ***Statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Astigmatism**: This occurs when the **cornea** or lens has an irregular shape, leading to blurred vision at all distances. It is corrected using **Cylindrical Lenses** that refract light differently in horizontal and vertical planes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lens Power**: The ability of a lens to refract light is measured in **Dioptres (D)**. The power (P) is the **reciprocal of the focal length** (f) in **metres** (P = 1/f).
 
• **Lens Formula**: The relationship between the object distance (u), image distance (v), and focal length (f) is given by **1/v - 1/u = 1/f**.
 
• **Presbyopia**: A condition associated with **age** (typically appearing after **40 years**), where the eye's natural lens loses **elasticity**, making it difficult to focus on close objects. It is often corrected with **Bifocal** or **Progressive lenses**.
 
• **Contact Lenses**: These work on the same principle of **refraction** but are placed directly on the **tear film** of the cornea.
</ul

questions.question: When a force is applied at 90circ to the direction of displacement of an object, the work done:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**is zero**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In physics, **Work Done** is defined as the product of the component of the **Force** in the direction of the **Displacement** and the magnitude of that displacement.
 
• The mathematical formula used to calculate work is **W = F s cos θ**, where **W** is the work done, **F** is the magnitude of the force applied, **s** is the displacement of the object, and **θ (theta)** is the **angle** between the force vector and the displacement vector.
 
• When a force is applied at an angle of **90 degrees** to the direction of displacement, it is considered **perpendicular**. In trigonometry, the value of **cos 90 degrees** is exactly **0**.
 
• Substituting this into the formula (**W = F x s x 0**), the resulting **Work Done** becomes **zero**. This indicates that the force does not contribute to the movement of the object in that specific direction. ***Hence, the statement that work done is zero is correct.***
 
• A practical example is a person walking on a flat road while carrying a **load** on their head. The force of **gravity** acts vertically downwards, while the displacement is horizontal (at a **90-degree angle**). Therefore, the work done by gravity on the load is **zero**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Positive Work**: This occurs when the **force** and the **displacement** are in the same direction, meaning the angle **θ** is **0 degrees** (or generally between 0 and 90). In this scenario, **cos θ** is positive, and the work done adds **kinetic energy** to the object.
 
• **Negative Work**: This happens when the force acts in the **opposite direction** to the displacement, such as when the angle **θ** is **180 degrees**. A common example is the force of **friction**, which opposes motion, resulting in a negative value because **cos 180 degrees** is **-1**.
 
• **SI Unit**: The standard **International System of Units** (SI) unit for work is the **Joule (J)**. One Joule is defined as the work done by a force of one **Newton (N)** causing a displacement of one **meter (m)**.
 
• **Scalar Nature**: Although both force and displacement are **vector quantities**, work done is a **scalar quantity**. This means it only has **magnitude** and no specific direction in space.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Centripetal Force**: In the case of **uniform circular motion**, the centripetal force is always directed towards the **center** of the circle, while the displacement is **tangential**. Because the angle between them is always **90 degrees**, the work done by the centripetal force is always **zero**.
 
• **Zero Displacement**: Even if a massive amount of **force** is applied, the work done is **zero** if the object does not move. For example, pushing against a **rigid stone wall** that does not budge results in no work being performed in the scientific sense.
 
• **Energy Transformation**: Work is a method of **energy transfer**. When **zero work** is done at a 90-degree angle, it signifies that no energy is being transferred into or out of the system by that particular force component.
 
• **Dimensions**: The dimensional formula for work is **[M1 L2 T-2]**, which is the same as the dimensional formula for **energy** and **torque**.

questions.question: Which component of blood serves as the fluid matrix in which cells are suspended?

The correct answer is __**Plasma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Blood** is a specialized **connective tissue** consisting of a **fluid matrix**, **plasma**, and **formed elements**.
 
• **Plasma** is the straw-colored, viscous fluid that constitutes nearly **55 per cent** of the total blood volume. It serves as the **fluid matrix** in which all the cellular components of blood are suspended. ***Hence, the correct option is Plasma.***
 
• Chemically, **plasma** is composed of about **90-92 per cent water**, while **proteins** contribute approximately **6-8 per cent** of its composition.
 
• The major proteins found in the plasma matrix include **Fibrinogens**, **Globulins**, and **Albumins**. **Fibrinogens** are essential for the **clotting or coagulation** of blood; **Globulins** are primarily involved in the **defense mechanisms** of the body; and **Albumins** help in maintaining **osmotic balance**.

• **Lumen**:
 
 
• In biology, a **Lumen** is the inside space of a tubular structure, such as an **artery** or **intestine**.
 
• In cellular biology, it can refer to the internal space of organelles like the **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)** or the **thylakoids** in chloroplasts.
 
 
 
• **Nucleoplasm**:
 
 
• **Nucleoplasm** is a type of **protoplasm** that is found within the **nucleus** of a cell, surrounded by the **nuclear envelope**.
 
• It serves as a suspension medium for the **nucleolus** and **chromatin** (DNA and proteins), facilitating **gene expression** and **DNA replication**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The term **protoplasm** is often used to describe the entire content of a live cell, including the **cytoplasm** and the **nucleus**.
 
• In **prokaryotic cells** (like bacteria), which lack a defined nucleus, the **cytoplasm** contains the primary genetic material (the **nucleoid**).
 
• The **cytoskeleton**, a network of protein fibers (microtubules and microfilaments), is located within the **cytoplasm** to provide structural support and aid in **intracellular transport**.
 
• The **cytoplasm** acts as a physical buffer, protecting the **genetic material** and **organelles** from damage caused by movement or collision with other cells.

questions.question: In plants, after fertilisation, the ovule develops into which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the life cycle of **flowering plants** (**Angiosperms**), the process of **fertilisation** triggers significant developmental changes in the floral organs.
 
• The **ovule**, which contains the female gametophyte, undergoes a series of transformations following the fusion of gametes and eventually develops into a **seed**. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• During this transition, the **integuments** (the protective outer layers of the ovule) harden and dry out to form the **seed coat** or **testa**, which protects the internal embryo.
 
• The **zygote**, formed by the fusion of one male gamete with the egg cell, divides and differentiates to become the **embryo**, which is the "baby plant" contained within the seed.
 
• While the ovules turn into seeds, the surrounding **ovary** grows in size and ripens to become the **fruit**, acting as a vessel for seed protection and dispersal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Double Fertilisation**: This is a characteristic feature of **Angiosperms**. It involves two fusions: one male gamete fuses with the egg (**Syngamy**) to form a **diploid zygote**, and the other fuses with **two polar nuclei** (**Triple Fusion**) to form a **triploid endosperm**.
 
• **Endosperm**: This tissue serves as a highly nutritious food store for the developing **embryo**. In some seeds, like **Castor**, the endosperm persists, while in others, like **Pea** and **Bean**, it is consumed during development.
 
• **Fruit vs. Seed**:
 
 
• The **fruit** is the ripened **ovary**.
 
• The **seed** is the ripened **ovule**.
 
 
 
• **Fruit Types**:
 
 
• **True Fruits**: Fruits that develop only from the **ovary** after fertilisation, such as **Mango** and **Grapes**.
 
• **False Fruits**: Fruits where other floral parts, like the **thalamus**, contribute to fruit formation, such as **Apple**, **Cashew**, and **Strawberry**.
 
• **Parthenocarpic Fruits**: Fruits that develop without fertilisation and are usually seedless, like **Banana**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **micropyle**, a small opening in the ovule, remains as a tiny pore in the **seed coat**. This is essential for the entry of **water** and **oxygen** during the process of **germination**.
 
• As the seed reaches maturity, its **water content** is significantly reduced, reaching about **10 to 15 percent** moisture by mass. 
 
• The embryo may enter a state of **dormancy**, which is a period of suspended growth that allows the seed to survive unfavorable environmental conditions until **germination** is possible.
 
• In **Gymnosperms**, seeds are produced but they are "naked" because they do not develop inside an **ovary**, and therefore, gymnosperms do not produce **fruits**.
</ul

__
 
• **Ultrasonography (USG)**, often called an ultrasound, is a primary diagnostic tool used during **pregnancy** to visualize the **fetus** and the **mother's reproductive organs**.
 
• Its main function is to **monitor the baby’s growth** and **development**, ensuring that the fetus is hitting appropriate **gestational milestones** based on the **date of conception**.
 
• A critical application of this technology is to **detect birth defects** or **congenital anomalies**. Structural issues related to the **heart, spine, brain, and limbs** can often be identified through detailed scans like the **Anomaly Scan** (usually performed between **18 to 22 weeks**).
 
• It is used to check the **position of the placenta**, the **amount of amniotic fluid**, and the **heartbeat of the fetus**, providing a comprehensive assessment of the pregnancy's health.
 
• Regarding the other options: It cannot determine the **blood group** of the baby (which requires **invasive procedures** like **amniocentesis** or **cordocentesis**), it is not used to measure **mother's weight** (done via a **weighing scale**), and while it can see the mother's organs, its primary routine use in pregnancy is not to check the **mother’s heartbeat** (which is monitored via **pulse** or **ECG**).

• **Mechanism of Action:** Ultrasonography works by emitting **high-frequency sound waves** (ultrasound) through a **transducer**. These waves bounce off internal structures and return as **echoes**, which a computer translates into **real-time images**.

• **2D Ultrasound:** The standard scan providing flat, **cross-sectional images** of the baby.
 
• **3D/4D Ultrasound:** Used to see **facial features** and **movements** in more detail; often used to detect specific **cleft lips** or **spinal defects**.
 
• **Doppler Ultrasound:** Used to measure the **blood flow** through the baby's **umbilical cord** and **heart**.
 
 
 
• **Safety:** Unlike **X-rays**, ultrasonography does not use **ionizing radiation**, making it safe for both the **mother** and the **developing fetus** when used by trained professionals.
 
• **Timelines:**
 
 
• **First Trimester (6-9 weeks):** Used for **dating** the pregnancy and confirming the **number of fetuses**.
 
• **Second Trimester (18-22 weeks):** The **Anomaly Scan** (Level II) is performed to check for **physical abnormalities**.
 
• **Third Trimester:** Used to check fetal **presentation** (position like **breech** or **cephalic**) before delivery.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: In a large population of sweet pea plants growing in stable conditions, which of the following best explains why genetic variation through sexual reproduction is still crucial for their long-term survival?

options.text: Variation helps sweet pea plants avoid cross-pollination, maintaining purity of the parental line.
Genetic variation ensures uniform flower color and height across future generations.
Hidden (recessive) alleles in sweet peas may offer resistance against future environmental stress.
Sweet pea plants reproduce faster sexually than asexually, ensuring more biomass production.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hidden (recessive) alleles in sweet peas may offer resistance against future environmental stress**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sexual reproduction** in **sweet pea plants** (***Pisum sativum***) is a fundamental process that facilitates **genetic recombination**. This process involves **meiosis**, where **crossing over** and **independent assortment** create unique combinations of **alleles** in offspring.
 
• In a **large population**, **recessive alleles** can remain "hidden" in **heterozygous** individuals (carriers). While these traits might not be beneficial in current **stable conditions**, they provide a **genetic reservoir** that may contain traits essential for survival if the environment changes, such as resistance to a new **pathogen** or **drought**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Maintaining "purity" through **self-pollination** or avoiding **cross-pollination** (Option 1) actually reduces **genetic diversity** and can lead to **inbreeding depression**, which weakens the long-term survival of the species. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Genetic variation** inherently promotes **diversity** and **phenotypic differences**, such as variations in **flower color**, **seed shape**, and **plant height**. It does not aim for **uniformity** (Option 2), which is more characteristic of **asexual reproduction** or **cloning**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• While sexual reproduction is vital for **evolution**, it is generally **slower** and more **energy-intensive** than **asexual reproduction**. **Biomass production** (Option 4) is usually maximized through rapid vegetative growth rather than the complex process of **gamete** formation and **fertilization**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mendelian Genetics:** **Gregor Mendel** conducted his historic experiments on **sweet peas** in the **1850s** and **1860s**. He identified that traits are inherited as discrete units (now known as **genes**) and established the **Law of Segregation** and the **Law of Independent Assortment**.
 
• **Gene Pool:** The total collection of **genes** and **alleles** in a **population** is called the **gene pool**. A large, diverse gene pool is a buffer against **extinction**, as it increases the likelihood that some individuals will possess the **traits** necessary to survive **environmental shifts**.
 
• **Heterozygote Advantage:** This occurs when an individual with a **heterozygous genotype** has higher **fitness** than those with **homozygous dominant** or **recessive genotypes**. This mechanism helps maintain **recessive alleles** within a population over **generations**.
 
• **Environmental Stressors:** These include **biotic factors** like **fungal infections** (e.g., **powdery mildew**) and **abiotic factors** like **soil salinity** or **temperature fluctuations**. **Genetic variation** ensures that the **sweet pea** population is not wiped out by a single adverse event.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Meiosis:** During **Prophase I** of **meiosis**, **homologous chromosomes** exchange segments (**crossing over**), ensuring that no two **gametes** are identical. This is the primary engine of **variation** in **sexually reproducing** organisms.
 
• **Long-term Survival vs. Short-term Efficiency:** **Sexual reproduction** may seem "wasteful" because it requires finding a **pollinator** or mate, but the **evolutionary** benefit of **adaptation** far outweighs the **metabolic costs** in **dynamic ecosystems**.
 
• **Population Size:** In **large populations**, the impact of **genetic drift** (random changes in **allele frequencies**) is minimized, allowing **natural selection** to act more effectively on the **variation** produced by **sexual reproduction**.
</ul

The volume of a solid cylinder is 6776 { cm}³ and its height is 44 { cm} . What is the total surface area of the solid cylinder?
 ( {Use } pi = (22)/(7) )

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Surface Area of a cylinder = 2πr(r + h), where π = 22/7.

The final result must be a multiple of 11 as it contains the factor 22.

Check divisibility by 11 (Difference of sum of digits at odd and even places):

Option (1) 2244: (2+4) − (2+4) = 0 (Divisible by 11).

Other options are not divisible by 11, so 2244 is the answer.

**∴ The correct answer is 2244 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Volume (V) = 6776 cm³, Height (h) = 44 cm

Formula Used: Volume = πr²h, Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2πr(r + h)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2bee465754282a9212ea3416c8203a4d26ea857f6991527b6b1347a9b08407f0.png] 

⇒ Volume = πr²h

⇒ 6776 = (22/7) × r² × 44

⇒ r² = (6776 × 7) / (22 × 44)

⇒ r² = 154 × 7 / 22 = 7 × 7

⇒ r = 7 cm

⇒ TSA = 2πr(r + h)

⇒ TSA = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × (7 + 44)

⇒ TSA = 44 × 51

⇒ TSA = 2244 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 2244 cm².**

Curved Surface Area of a Cylinder

It is the area of the curved surface only, excluding the top and bottom circles. Formula: CSA = 2πrh.

Volume of a Cylinder

It is the total space occupied by the cylinder. Formula: Volume = πr²h.

Total Surface Area of a Cylinder

It is the sum of the curved surface area and the areas of the two circular bases. Formula: TSA = 2πr(r + h).

Radius and Diameter Relation

The diameter (d) of the circular base is always twice the radius (r). Formula: d = 2r.</p

questions.question: Nilu covers a distance by walking for 6 h. While returning, her speed decreases by 2 km/h and she takes 9 h to cover the same distance. What was her speed while returning?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Distance is constant ∴ Speed ratio is the inverse of Time ratio.

Time ratio (Forward : Return) = 6 : 9 = 2 : 3

Speed ratio (Forward : Return) = 3 : 2

Speed difference = 3 − 2 = 1 unit → 2 km/h

Return speed = 2 units = 2 × 2 = 4 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 4 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken while walking forward (T₁) = 6 h

Time taken while returning (T₂) = 9 h

Decrease in speed = 2 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/649f451a42f6f3386753d7812a88b68e79ba211adabef2a219dfd138e4339d10.png] 

⇒ Let the initial speed while walking forward be S km/h.

⇒ Distance covered = Speed × Time = S × 6 = 6S

⇒ Returning speed = (S − 2) km/h

⇒ Distance covered while returning = (S − 2) × 9 = 9(S − 2)

⇒ Since the distance is the same for both journeys:

⇒ 6S = 9(S − 2)

⇒ 6S = 9S − 18

⇒ 18 = 9S − 6S

⇒ 18 = 3S

⇒ S = 18 ÷ 3 = 6 km/h

⇒ Returning speed = S − 2 = 6 − 2 = 4 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 4 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Relationship

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂).

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If an object covers equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed is 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5 ÷ 18.</p

questions.question: In an equilateral triangle ABC, point D lies on side BC such that, 3BD = BC. Which of the following relations is correct?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In an equilateral triangle ABC of side 'a', if a point D divides side BC such that BD = a/n,

The relation is given by the formula: n²AD² = (n² − n + 1)AB².

Here, 3BD = BC ⇒ BD = BC/3, so n = 3.

Substituting n = 3: 3²AD² = (3² − 3 + 1)AB²

9AD² = (9 − 3 + 1)AB² ⇒ 9AD² = 7AB².

**∴ The correct answer is 9AD²=7AB².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ΔABC is equilateral, so AB = BC = CA. Point D is on BC such that BD = BC/3.

**Formula Used:** Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular².

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/155965f29ecb4ee49e473904ab2781e7b54dc1e3ac215d65cc5f738a3a45523f.png] 

Let the side of the equilateral triangle AB = BC = CA = a.

Draw altitude AM ⊥ BC. In an equilateral triangle, altitude bisects the base.

⇒ BM = MC = BC/2 = a/2.

⇒ AM = √(AB² − BM²) = √(a² − (a/2)²) = √(3a²/4) = (√3/2)a.

Given BD = BC/3 = a/3.

⇒ DM = BM − BD = a/2 − a/3 = (3a − 2a)/6 = a/6.

In right-angled ΔADM, apply Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ AD² = AM² + DM²

⇒ AD² = [(√3/2)a]² + (a/6)²

⇒ AD² = 3a²/4 + a²/36

⇒ AD² = (27a² + a²) / 36

⇒ AD² = 28a² / 36 = 7a² / 9

⇒ 9AD² = 7a²

Since a = AB:

⇒ 9AD² = 7AB².

**∴ The correct answer is 9AD²=7AB².**

**__Additional Information__**

Height of Equilateral Triangle

The altitude or height (h) of an equilateral triangle with side 'a' is always (√3/2)×a.

Area of Equilateral Triangle

The area is given by (√3/4)×a², where 'a' is the length of the side.

Inradius and Circumradius

For side 'a', the Inradius (r) is a/(2√3) and the Circumradius (R) is a/√3. Note that R = 2r.

Apollonius Theorem

For any triangle with side AB, AC and median AD on BC: AB² + AC² = 2(AD² + BD²).</p

questions.question: A person covers a certain distance with a speed of 17 km/h in 8 min. If he wants to cover the same distance in 5 min, what should be his speed?

questions.question: A basket contains 96 fruits consisting of mangoes and oranges. If there are 42 more mangoes than oranges, then how many mangoes are there?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the quantity of the larger value when the sum and difference are known:

Quantity of Mangoes = (Sum of fruits + Difference) ÷ 2

Quantity of Mangoes = (96 + 42) ÷ 2

Quantity of Mangoes = 138 ÷ 2 = 69

**∴ The correct answer is 69.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total fruits (Mangoes + Oranges) = 96

Difference (Mangoes − Oranges) = 42

**Method:** Linear Equation in One Variable

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e583d63f186cb88a687e1d99ca6e05b4c7d247f0519023095c4bf4870adb62a0.png] 

Let the number of Oranges be x.

Then, the number of Mangoes = x + 42

According to the question:

⇒ x + (x + 42) = 96

⇒ 2x + 42 = 96

⇒ 2x = 96 − 42

⇒ 2x = 54

⇒ x = 54 ÷ 2

⇒ x = 27 (Number of Oranges)

⇒ Number of Mangoes = 27 + 42 = 69

**∴ The correct answer is 69.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum and Difference Formula

If the sum (S) and difference (D) of two numbers are known, the larger number is (S+D)÷2 and the smaller number is (S−D)÷2.

Linear Equations

Equations in the form ax + b = c are solved by isolating the variable x through inverse operations on both sides.

Ratio from Sum and Difference

The ratio of the two numbers can be calculated directly as (S+D) : (S−D). Here, Ratio = (96+42) : (96−42) = 138 : 54 = 23 : 9.</p

questions.question: The simplified value of (x - (1)/(x)) (x + (1)/(x)) (x² + (1)/(x²)) (x⁴ + (1)/(x⁴)) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the identity (a − b)(a + b) = a² − b² successively to the terms.

(x − 1/x)(x + 1/x) = x² − 1/x²

(x² − 1/x²)(x² + 1/x²) = x⁴ − 1/x⁴

(x⁴ − 1/x⁴)(x⁴ + 1/x⁴) = x⁸ − 1/x⁸

**∴ The correct answer is (x⁸ − 1/x⁸).**

⇒ (x − 1/x) × (x + 1/x) = x² − (1/x)² = x² − 1/x²

⇒ Multiplying the result with the third bracket:

⇒ (x² − 1/x²) × (x² + 1/x²) = (x²)² − (1/x²)² = x⁴ − 1/x⁴

⇒ Multiplying the result with the fourth bracket:

⇒ (x⁴ − 1/x⁴) × (x⁴ + 1/x⁴) = (x⁴)² − (1/x⁴)² = x⁸ − 1/x⁸

**∴ The correct answer is (x⁸ − 1/x⁸).**

Power of a Power Rule

questions.question: If sin θ = 3/5, then find the value of cos θ.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The trigonometric ratio sin θ = 3/5 corresponds to Perpendicular / Hypotenuse.

Recognize the fundamental Pythagorean triplet: (3, 4, 5).

In this triplet, if Perpendicular = 3 and Hypotenuse = 5, then Base must be 4.

Using the ratio cos θ = Base / Hypotenuse, we get cos θ = 4/5.

**∴ The correct answer is 4/5.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: sin θ = 3/5

Formula: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e9032e3a0e2ac04a2afce950528257db68556cd614106a5441319a87120338eb.png] 

⇒ cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ

⇒ cos θ = √(1 − (3/5)²)

⇒ cos θ = √(1 − 9/25)

⇒ cos θ = √((25 − 9) / 25)

⇒ cos θ = √(16/25)

⇒ cos θ = 4/5

**∴ The correct answer is 4/5.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

The primary identity is sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, from which we derive cos θ = √(1 − sin²θ).

Pythagorean Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, Base² + Perpendicular² = Hypotenuse².

Pythagorean Triplets

Common triplets used in exams include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25).

Ratio Definitions

sin θ = P/H, cos θ = B/H, tan θ = P/B, cot θ = B/P, sec θ = H/B, cosec θ = H/P.</p

questions.question:
Four times the present age of Anil is equal to five times the present age of Bhavya.
After 6 years, the age of Bhavya will be 6 years less than twice the present age of Anil.
What is the difference (in years) between their present ages?
questions.solution:

Ratio of Anil (A) to Bhavya (B) present ages = 5 : 4

Let present ages be 5x and 4x.

According to question: (4x + 6) = 2 × (5x) − 6

⇒ 4x + 6 = 10x − 6

⇒ 6x = 12 ⇒ x = 2

Difference between their ages = 5x − 4x = x = 2 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ (B + 6) = 2A − 6

⇒ (4A/5) + 6 = 2A − 6

⇒ 4A/5 + 12 = 2A

⇒ 12 = 2A − 0.8A

⇒ 1.2A = 12

⇒ A = 10 years

⇒ B = (4 × 10)/5 = 8 years

⇒ Difference = 10 − 8 = 2 years

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two people remains the same regardless of how many years pass.

Ratio to Value Conversion

If two quantities are in the ratio x : y, they can be represented as kx and ky, where k is the common multiplier.

Future and Past Ages

If current age is X, age after n years is (X + n) and age n years ago was (X − n).</p

questions.question: In April 2025, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) came out with the operational framework for PaRRVA. What is the purpose of PaRRVA?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)** introduced the operational framework for the **Performance Reporting and Rating Verification Agency (PaRRVA)** in **April 2025** to bring transparency to the investment ecosystem.
 
• The primary objective of **PaRRVA** is the **verification of investment performance claims** made by regulated intermediaries, such as **Investment Advisers (IAs)** and **Research Analysts (RAs)**, ensuring they do not mislead investors with inflated return data. ***Hence, the correct answer is Verifying investment performance claims.***
 
• Under this framework, any performance-related claims made in advertisements or marketing materials must be validated by **PaRRVA** before being circulated to the public.
 
• The agency is designed to act as an **independent body** (often supported by subsidiaries of **Stock Exchanges**) that checks the authenticity of historical data and the methodology used to calculate returns.
 
• By mandating this verification, **SEBI** aims to curb the practice of "cherry-picking" profitable periods or using "back-tested" data to lure unsuspecting retail investors into risky financial products.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI):**
 
 
• **SEBI** was established on **April 12, 1988**, and was given statutory powers on **January 30, 1992**, through the **SEBI Act, 1992**.
 
• It is the principal regulator for the securities market in **India**, headquartered in **Mumbai**, with regional offices in **New Delhi**, **Kolkata**, **Chennai**, and **Ahmedabad**.
 
• The main functions of **SEBI** include protecting the interests of investors, regulating the business in stock exchanges, and promoting the development of the securities market.
 
 
 
• **Investment Advisers and Research Analysts:**
 
 
• These entities are regulated under the **SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013** and **SEBI (Research Analysts) Regulations, 2014**.
 
• They are prohibited from making **guaranteed return** claims or using superlative terms like "best" or "No. 1" without objective verification by bodies like **PaRRVA**.
 
 
 
• **Investor Protection Measures:**
 
 
• The introduction of **PaRRVA** is a step towards **investor protection**, preventing financial fraud and mis-selling in the growing digital investment advisory space.
 
• It complements other **SEBI** initiatives like the **SCORES** (SEBI Complaints Redress System) platform, which allows investors to lodge grievances against listed companies and intermediaries online.
 
 
 
• **Digital Transformation in Regulation:**
 
 
• The **PaRRVA** framework utilizes **algorithmic verification** and data feeds from **Depositories** and **Exchanges** to ensure that the reported performance matches actual transaction records.
 
• This move aligns with global best practices in financial regulation, where **independent audits** of performance track records are becoming standard for wealth management firms.
 
 
</ul

• **Account Freezing Rules:** **RBI** has reiterated that accounts should not be frozen routinely without providing adequate notice and multiple reminders to the customer regarding **KYC** pendency.

• The original **2011 Guidelines** were issued by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** to provide a framework for designating buffer zones around **National Parks** and **Wildlife Sanctuaries**.
 
• The decision to revise the guidelines stems from the need to streamline the **ESZ notification process** and address the administrative and legal challenges faced over the last decade.

• The board is chaired by the **Prime Minister of India**, while the **Standing Committee** is chaired by the **Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change**.
 
• It serves as the apex body for all **wildlife-related matters**, including the approval of projects inside and around **Protected Areas**.
 
 
 
• **Eco-Sensitive Zones (ESZ):**
 
 
• ESZs are areas notified by the **MoEFCC** under the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**.
 
• The primary objective is to create "**shock absorbers**" for protected areas by regulating human activities in the immediate vicinity.
 
• Generally, an **ESZ** can extend up to **10 kilometers** around a **National Park** or **Wildlife Sanctuary**, though this distance can be increased or decreased based on specific ecological requirements.

• **Regulated Activities:** These include the **felling of trees**, establishment of **hotels and resorts**, drastic change of agriculture systems, and the commercial use of **natural water resources**.
 
• **Permitted Activities:** These include **ongoing agriculture** and **horticulture practices** by local communities, **rainwater harvesting**, and the use of **renewable energy sources**.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Interventions:** In **2022**, the **Supreme Court of India** mandated a minimum **1 km ESZ** for all protected areas, though this was later modified in **2023** to allow for area-specific flexibility, emphasizing that **rigid boundaries** may not be practical for every geographical location.

questions.question: What was the theme of India’s 76th Republic Day celebrated on 26 January 2025?

options.text: Atmanirbhar Bharat: Udaan Nayi Soch Ki

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swarnim Bharat: Virasat aur Vikas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India celebrated its **76th Republic Day** on **January 26, 2025**, with great fervor and national pride.
 
• The central theme for the **2025** celebrations was **"Swarnim Bharat: Virasat aur Vikas"**, which translates to **"Golden India: Heritage and Development"**.
 
• The theme was chosen to reflect India's dual commitment to preserving its rich **cultural heritage** (Virasat) while striving for rapid **modern development** (Vikas) towards the goal of **Viksit Bharat by 2047**.
 
• The Republic Day parade was held at the iconic **Kartavya Path** in **New Delhi**, showcasing the nation's military prowess, indigenous defense equipment, and diverse cultural tableaux.
 
• The celebration marked the **75th anniversary** of the adoption of the **Constitution of India**, emphasizing the strength of Indian democracy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Significance:** Republic Day commemorates the date on which the **Constitution of India** came into effect on **January 26, 1950**. While the Constitution was adopted on **November 26, 1949**, the **26th of January** was chosen because it was on this day in **1930** that the **Purna Swaraj** (Complete Independence) declaration was promulgated by the **Indian National Congress**.
 
• **Viksit Bharat @2047:** This is the government's vision to transform India into a **developed nation** by the **centenary of its independence** in **2047**. The **2025 theme** aligns with this long-term objective of economic growth and global leadership.
 
• **Chief Guest Tradition:** Every year, India invites a world leader as the **Chief Guest** for the Republic Day parade. For the **2025** celebrations, **President Mohamed Muizzu** of the **Maldives** was invited, highlighting India's **"Neighborhood First"** policy and maritime security cooperation.
 
• **Previous Themes:** In **2024**, during the **75th Republic Day**, the themes were **"Viksit Bharat"** and **"Bharat - Loktantra ki Matruka"** (India - Mother of Democracy), focusing on women-led development and democratic values.
 
• **Beating Retreat Ceremony:** The Republic Day festivities conclude with the **Beating Retreat** ceremony on the evening of **January 29** at **Vijay Chowk**, featuring performances by the bands of the **Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Constitutional Head:** The **President of India**, currently **Droupadi Murmu**, unfurls the **National Flag** and takes the salute during the parade, as the President is the **Constitutional Head** of the State.
 
• **Padma Awards:** On the eve of Republic Day, the **Government of India** announces the **Padma Awards**, which are among the highest civilian honors in the country, categorized into **Padma Vibhushan**, **Padma Bhushan**, and **Padma Shri**.
 
• **Atmanirbhar Bharat:** Recent parades have emphasized **indigenization**, featuring only **Made-in-India** weapon systems like the **LCH Prachand**, **K-9 Vajra**, and **Nag** anti-tank guided missiles to showcase self-reliance in defense.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following volcanoes, located in Ethiopia, was in the news in November 2025 for erupting for the first time in recorded history?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hayli Gubbi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hayli Gubbi** is a **shield volcano** located at the southern end of the **Erta Ale volcanic range** in the **Afar Region** of **Ethiopia**.
 
• In **November 2025**, the volcano garnered significant attention from the global scientific community after it erupted for the **first time in recorded history**. Prior to this event, the volcano was primarily known for its **fumarolic activity** and was considered relatively quiet compared to its neighbors.
 
• The volcano reaches an **elevation** of approximately **521 meters** (**1,709 feet**) and is situated within the **Danakil Depression**, a tectonic plate junction that is one of the lowest and hottest places on **Earth**.
 
• This eruption is geologically significant because it provides new evidence regarding the **magmatic processes** occurring within the **Afar Triple Junction**, where the **Nubian**, **Somali**, and **Arabian tectonic plates** are pulling away from each other.
 
• Volcanologists monitor this region closely as the **Erta Ale range** is one of the most active volcanic chains in **Africa**, though **Hayli Gubbi** specifically had no prior historical record of a major **lava-producing eruption**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mount Semeru:**
 
 
• Located in **East Java**, **Indonesia**, **Mount Semeru** is the highest mountain on the island of **Java**.
 
• It is an active **stratovolcano** known for its frequent eruptions, often producing **pyroclastic flows** and **lahars** that pose significant risks to local populations.
 
• It is a prominent feature of the **Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park** and has been erupting almost continuously since **1967**.
 
 
 
• **Kilauea:**
 
 
• Situated on the **Big Island** of **Hawaii**, **USA**, **Kilauea** is one of the most active **shield volcanoes** in the world.
 
• It is a **hotspot volcano**, meaning it is not located on a plate boundary but over a plume of **magma** rising through the **Earth's crust**.
 
• It is famous for its **effusive eruptions** and long-standing **lava lakes**, and it is a central part of the **Hawaii Volcanoes National Park**.
 
 
 
• **Krasheninnikov:**
 
 
• This is a complex **volcanic system** located on the **Kamchatka Peninsula** in **Russia**.
 
• It consists of two overlapping **stratovolcanoes** housed within a large **caldera** formed during the **late Pleistocene** epoch.
 
• The **Kamchatka** region is part of the **Pacific Ring of Fire** and contains one of the highest concentrations of active volcanoes in the world.
 
 
 
• **Volcanism in Ethiopia:**
 
 
• **Ethiopia** is home to more than **60 volcanoes**, many of which are located along the **Great Rift Valley**.
 
• The **Erta Ale** volcano, also in the **Afar region**, is the most famous in the country, known for its persistent **lava lake** that has been active for decades.
 
• The **tectonic activity** in this region is slowly splitting the **African continent** apart, a process that will eventually lead to the formation of a new **ocean basin**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geological Context:** The eruption of **Hayli Gubbi** in **2025** serves as a reminder of the unpredictable nature of **dormant volcanoes** in **rift zones**.
 
• **Data Monitoring:** Modern **satellite technology** and **seismic sensors** allow researchers to detect changes in **ground deformation** and **gas emissions**, which preceded the historical eruption of this Ethiopian volcano.
 
• **Afar Triangle:** This region is unique because it is the only place on **Earth** where a **mid-ocean ridge** can be studied on land, making the activity of volcanoes like **Hayli Gubbi** vital for **geophysical research**.
</ul
